newsitem.title: DENMARK: Lego 1996 profits up, hopes for new products boost.
newsitem.headline: Lego 1996 profits up, hopes for new products boost.

text.p: Lego group, maker of children's plastic building bricks, Monday posted slightly higher profits for 1996.

Pre-tax profit rose to 699 million crowns ($106 million) from the previous year's 676 million crowns while net profit gained 9 percent to 470 million crowns on 10 percent higher revenues of 7.5 billion crowns.

It said sales growth in North America, Britain , Benelux and Russia helped bolster profits, with the United States, Canada and Mexico together noting a healthy 26 percent rise in turnover, while overseas markets in South Korea and Japan stagnated.

"Among the reasons for the low rate of increase are the increased investment in product development, including software, and the costs incurred as a result of the restructuring process," Chief Executive Kjeld Kirk Kristiansen said in a statement.
Kristiansen said that Lego's main activity would continue to be bricks and construction toys and dismissed media rumours that it planned to abandon bricks for digital products.
"The world's children and their parents and grandparents are not tired of building and designing with Lego bricks. Far from it," Kristiansen said.

Lego said more new products were being launched in 1997 than ever before with over 40 percent of the product range renewed and great expectations pinned to a new Lego Scala flexible doll house system and a Lego CD-ROM Technic set.
